issues_confirmed: standalone/places_scraper.py:38,64 — only raise_for_status() is called; the Google Places JSON 'status' field (REQUEST_DENIED / OVER_QUERY_LIMIT / INVALID_REQUEST, all returned with HTTP 200) is never read. grep for 'status' in places_scraper.py matches only raise_for_status.

standalone/places_scraper.py:195 — mark_done() is called unconditionally after the per-place loop, so an area that returned zero results because of an API error is recorded as scraped; standalone/area_manager.py:13-22 then skips it for rescrape_days (default 30), poisoning --resume.
standalone/places_scraper.py:47-54 — pagination sleeps a fixed 2s before reusing next_page_token and does not detect INVALID_REQUEST, so a not-yet-warm token silently truncates results from 60 to 20.

standalone/cli.py:311-377 — the CLI send command has no daily-cap check, while standalone/web_server.py:484-488 and :516 enforce _daily_cap()/_sent_today() on the web path. The root README's Workflow section instructs the client to use the uncapped CLI path.

standalone/email_sender.py:114-115 — every exception (timeout, transient 4xx) returns success:False; callers at standalone/web_server.py:523 and standalone/cli.py:359 write email_status='bounced', which is permanent because the send query requires email_status=='pending' (web_server.py:458, cli.py:332) and /contacts/{id}/reset (web_server.py:214-225) only clears 'approved'.
standalone/web_server.py:248,280-292 — /contacts/duplicates loads all traders into memory and runs a full pairwise SequenceMatcher comparison, O(n^2), against a stated target of 10,000+ traders.

README.md (release section, 'First-time Gist setup' steps 1-2 and release step 7) still names the manifest file version.json, but standalone/update_checker.py:15 was changed to Supplier_Scraper.json in commit a08e1a3 precisely because the old name 404'd silently; update_checker.py:47-48 swallows all errors.

standalone/cities_us.txt — 13 duplicate city lines out of 267 (Akron OH, Arvada CO, Billings MT, Costa Mesa CA, Eugene OR, Glendale CA, Henderson NV, Inglewood CA, Lansing MI, Palmdale CA, Peoria IL, Rancho Cucamonga CA, Tallahassee FL); each wastes a Text Search call per term against the 10k/month cap in billing_guard.py:24-25.
standalone/billing_guard.py:64 — the counter is incremented before the HTTP request is made, so failed requests still consume free-tier budget.
standalone/website_email_extractor.py:29,44 — up to 6 sequential fetches at 8s timeout each (~48s worst case per place), and the worst case is the no-email path whose result is discarded.
standalone/web_server.py:66-70 — the _setup_guard middleware re-reads and re-parses config.ini from disk on every HTTP request.
standalone/validator.py:40 — returns True when no Hunter.io/ZeroBounce key is configured, so email_valid means 'unchecked', not 'verified'.

backend/ and frontend/ are unreferenced by standalone/; backend/requirements.txt pins python-jose==3.3.0, pillow==10.3.0, scrapy==2.11.1, selenium==4.21.0, sendgrid==6.11.0 and frontend/ has no lockfile.

verdict: Healthy and genuinely shipped — clean small modules, real tests, working end-to-end product — but the scraper's total blindness to Google's JSON error statuses means the one workflow it exists for (the full US run) can fail silently and lock itself out of retrying for 30 days. Fix that before the next scrape.
